intro.description: Two short STAR cases. One method: change one factor, observe the response, and make the next step clear.
intro.casesHint: Click a case or start Presentation Mode when you are ready to speak.

slides.label: Overflow / Task
slides.title: The system had to become stable.
slides.short: Change one factor at a time
slides.description: I changed the packing structure while keeping the flow conditions fixed. The task was to understand why the same setup behaved differently.

slides.label: Overflow / Action
slides.title: Observe. Identify. Verify.
slides.description: I used a simple control loop instead of changing many things at once.

resultButtons.label: Operation variable
resultButtons.text: Packing structure changed. Flow conditions stayed fixed.

resultButtons.label: What I saw
resultButtons.text: When resistance became too high, liquid came out from the top.

resultButtons.label: What I changed
resultButtons.text: I adjusted liquid flow in the same overflow-prone experiment.

resultButtons.label: What changed
resultButtons.text: The overflow stopped, so I used flow as a control variable.

slides.label: Overflow / Result
slides.title: The overflow disappeared.
slides.description: After I adjusted the liquid flow in the same overflow-prone experiment, the overflow stopped. I then treated flow as a control variable and continued the comparison.

slides.label: Team / Task
slides.title: One RPB. Two research tasks.
slides.description: I shared the overflow finding with the project student. We needed to organize the setup and use the same equipment without losing the research sequence.

slides.label: Team / Action
slides.title: Organize. Teach. Coordinate.
slides.description: I helped assemble the experimental setup, explained the operating sequence, and coordinated the shared equipment around the two tasks.

slides.label: Team / Result
slides.title: Progress became a team result.
slides.description: The student completed the thesis project and received a competition award. My contribution was the structure, equipment guidance, and coordination around the work.

closing.title: Make the equipment state clear. Make the next action clear.
closing.text: That is how I would contribute as an Equipment Engineer while following safety rules, SOPs, records, and escalation paths.

systems.title: System thinking
systems.body: Change one factor, keep the rest steady, and read the equipment response.

evidence.title: Evidence first
evidence.body: Separate what I saw from what the literature may explain.

people.title: Team coordination
people.body: Share the finding, make the next step clear, and keep the handoff visible.
